question.text: This Canadian province held sovereignty referendums in 1980 and 1995 because many of its residents want to become an independent country. Unlike residents in other provinces, most of its residents speak French.
question.clue: Its populace voted in 1980 and 1995 on referendums brought by its provincial "Parti", and a namesake "Bloc" represents it federally.

swap.text: This province is the most populous and borders both Minnesota and New York. The capital Ottawa and the major city of Toronto both lie in this province.
swap.clue: The First Nations leader Tecumseh was killed in this province during the Battle of the Thames (TIMS) in the War of 1812.

question.text: A Quebecois ["que-beck-WAA"] prime minister of Canada with this last name invoked the War Measures Act for the third time in history to end the October Crisis. His son with this surname won a third term as Canadian prime minister in 2021 federal elections.
question.answerHtml: Trudeau [accept Pierre Trudeau or Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliot Trudeau or Justin Trudeau or Justin Pierre James Trudeau]
question.clue: Another politician with this name initiated the Phoenix Pay system, and was given the nickname "little potato" when attending a G20 summit in China.

swap.leadin: The sign language used by this group is considered severely endangered, with less than forty native speakers worldwide.
swap.text: Name this ethnic group that is indigenous to the arctic regions of Greenland and North America. They are known for their use of kayaks and dog sleds in transportation and hunting.
swap.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

question.leadin: This man was accused of metaphorically urinating on a rug after giving a speech in Philadelphia in 1965 where he questioned U.S. foreign policy.
question.text: Name this Canadian prime minister, who earlier won a Nobel Peace Prize for negotiating an end to the Suez Crisis.
question.clue: This successor to Louis St. Laurent as party leader accepted the Bomarc missile program and instituted universal healthcare.

swap.leadin: This man established a provisional government that tried and executed Thomas Scott, after which the Wolseley Expedition was dispatched to put down a rebellion led by this man.
swap.text: Name this Metis leader who instigated the Red River Rebellion in 1869. This man was hanged after he led the North-West Rebellion in 1885.
swap.clue: This man was captured with the Cree Chief Poundmaker during the Battle of Batoche, and he appointed a tribunal which sentenced Thomas Scott to death.

question.text: The nickname "Old Ironsides" came from now-captain Isaac Hull's victory over the Guerriere at the start of the War of 1812. The Guerriere had been heading for this British Atlantic port, now the capital of Nova Scotia.
question.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

swap.leadin: Accusations of vote-buying in this scandal led to the swift introduction of a secret ballot by the next government.
swap.text: Name this scandal in which Hugh Allan bribed lawmakers to win a contract to build a railroad. It led to the downfall of John Macdonald's government.
swap.clue: Shortly after this event, secret ballots were introduced and Sandford Fleming was appointed by the Department of Public Works to ensure that certain parts of an enterprise were built publicly.

question.text: The SNC-Lavalin affair is causing problems for this party in the 2019 election, and could help other parties, such as the Conservatives or the NDP win. This is the party of Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.
question.answerHtml: Liberal Party of Canada [accept Parti libéral du Canada]
question.clue: A request to dissolve parliament by a leader of this party was refused by Governor-General Julian Byng in 1926.

swap.leadin: Louis Montcalm led French forces at this battle, which was the site of a Benjamin West painting depicting The Death of General Wolfe.
swap.text: Name this battle during the French and Indian War, which was followed up by the bloodier Battle of Sainte-Foy.
swap.answer: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
swap.clue: It resulted in the death of both commanders: for the French, the Marquis de Montcalm, and for the British, James Wolfe.

question.leadin: This group's advocacy prompted the Canadian government to request a clarification for Section 24 of the British North America Act, 1867.
question.text: Name this group of women's rights activists who were the petitioners in the Persons case. This group, which included Irene Parlby and Louise McKinney, is also named after the western province where they initially convened.

swap.leadin: This province was the site of a 1962 strike mediated by Lord Taylor.
swap.text: Name this Canadian province whose long-time Premier, Tommy Douglas, was named the "Greatest Canadian" in a 2004 poll.
swap.clue: Mounties fought workers who had been left in this province as leaders of the On-to-Ottawa trek went to meet the PM.

question.text: This Frenchman explored the Gulf of St. Lawrence and the St. Lawrence rivers, and is credited with giving Canada its present name.
question.clue: On their second voyage, this person made contact with the residents of the village of Stadacona.

swap.leadin: This organization kidnapped James Cross and killed Pierre Laporte.
swap.text: Name this organization whose actions led to the October Crisis.
swap.answerHtml: Front de libération du Québec (or FLQ, or Felquistes, or Quebec Liberation Front)
swap.clue: Members of this group kidnapped British Trade Commissioner James Cross and Minister of Labour and Immigration Pierre Laporte.

question.leadin: These people may have inspired the tuniit("toon-EAT"), a race of giants in a successor culture's mythology.
question.text: Name this archaeological culture, which preceded the Thule people in northern Canada and Greenland. Bows and arrows are conspicuously absent from their sites despite their use by the previous Saqqaq ("sah-KAHK") culture.
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.leadin: The Canadian Bill of Rights, which was Canada's first federal law to protect human rights, was passed during the administration of this prime minister.
swap.text: Name this prime minister of Canada who led the Progressive Conservative Party. This prime minister controversially cancelled the Avro Arrow program and accepted Bomarc missiles from the United States.
swap.clue: He also cancelled the Avro Arrow program, halting production of fighter jets in his country, when he signed NORAD with the US. Raised in Saskatchewan, he passed his country's Bill of Rights, and presided over the opening of the St. Lawrence Seaway.

question.text: In 1953, Mowat was falsely accused of having made up the Ihalmiut by Jean Lesage. Lesage's 1960 election as premier marked the start of this historical period of secularization and welfare state formation.
question.clue: (+) The beginning of this movement was signaled by the Union Nationale's loss in 1960 elections to the Liberal Party led by Jean Lesage.

swap.text: This Liberal Prime Minister from 1948-57 enthusiastically got Canada on board NATO, expanded social security, and directed his Secretary of State for External Affairs, Lester Pearson, to resolve the Suez Crisis.
swap.answerHtml: Louis St. Laurent [or Louis Stephen St. Laurent; or Louis-Etienne St-Laurent]
swap.clue: This Canadian Prime Minister preceded John Diefenbaker. This Prime Minister helped establish NATO, while his foreign affairs minister Lester Pearson helped broker the Suez Crisis.

question.leadin: This man worked with the Baring Brothers to secure financial backing for a railroad that connected Halifax to Windsor.
question.text: Name this publisher of the Novascotian and Morning Chronicle who accused local politicians of stealing over 30,000 pounds from the public treasury, then was acquitted in a landmark 1835 trial affirming the freedom of the press in Canada.

swap.leadin: This rebellion began with the defeat of Leif Crozier by troops under Gabriel Dumont at Duck Lake.
swap.text: Name this Metis rebellion in Saskatchewan that ended at the Battle of Batoche. The Cree Indians Poundmaker and Big Bear were part of this rebellion.
swap.answerHtml: North-West Rebellion [or Saskatchewan Rebellion; or Northwest Uprising; or Second Riel Rebellion]
